applies_to: Contemporary Controls BAST-221C and BAST-221CH (with humidity) wired thermostats for multi-stage heating, cooling and ventilation, such as rooftop units.
summary: The BAST-221C-B2 is the wired BACnet MS/TP version of the BASstat multi-stage thermostat for up to two cooling and two heating stages plus fan. The 221CH version adds humidity and dew point readings. It exposes temperatures, setpoints, system and fan modes, occupancy, relay control and status, and setup values as BACnet objects.
notes: From the BACnet Object Table (manual pages 26-34). The table is shared across the BASstat family; rows printed in grey (objects this model does not use) are left out.
Access is from the Readable/Writable column; R/W objects are shown as writable.
Temperature objects follow the Temperature Scale object (BV 6: 0 = °C, 1 = °F).

Compared with the Wi-Fi BW2 version, AV 20 is the MS/TP MAC address, Device Instance moves to AV 21, MV 6 is Baud Rate, Display Options / Control Type shift to MV 7 / MV 8, BV 3 (auto fan speed style) is listed and AV 39 / AV 40 are greyed out.
Control Type (MV 8) prints states 1 and 4 in grey with a note that cool-only and heat-only are disabled; Lowest Fan Speed and Fan Speed Status print Med and Hi in grey.
Current Humidity (AI 4), Current Dew Point (AI 5) and Humidity Offset (AV 22) are on the 221CH model only. The AV 23 name is printed as "Cooling Short Cycle" at a page break.

source.title: BAST-221C/CH-B2 BACnet Communicating Thermostat for Multi-Stage Heating/Cooling/Ventilation User Manual

integration.summary: Turn the thermostat outputs on with On-Off Control (BV 5), set occupancy with Occupancy Command (BV 14), and write the system mode, cooling and heating setpoints and fan mode. Read the space temperature, occupancy status, output status and fan speed.
integration.enable: On-Off Control (BV 5) switches the thermostat outputs. Occupancy Command (BV 14) only takes effect when the ESI contact is disabled in Lock (AV 18 bit value 64); by default occupancy comes from the ESI dry contact.
integration.heartbeat: A space temperature written to Space Temperature Via BACnet (AV 1) is only used while the BMS keeps toggling Heartbeat Signal (BV 16) within the Heartbeat Rate (AV 29) period, in seconds; otherwise the thermostat reverts to its own sensor.
integration.remote_sensors: Set Temperature Source (MV 3) to 3 (Assigned through BACnet) and write the space temperature to AV 1, toggling BV 16 as a heartbeat.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only: MAC address 1-127 from the Engineering menu (Addr) or the MAC Address object; baud 9600-76800 from the bAud menu item or Baud Rate (MV 6), 38400 by default.
Device instance = devH x 1000 + devL in the Engineering menu, or write Device Instance (AV 21) once online.
Changing the MAC address, baud or device instance over BACnet needs the comms-parameter lock in Lock (AV 18, bit value 256) cleared first.
The manual gives 100001 as the default device instance, MAC address 1 and 38400 baud.
gotchas: Lock (AV 18) is bit-coded: add the bit values to lock buttons, ignore the ESI or door contact, block changes to the comms settings or hand the relays to BACnet (512).
The manual text calls the Lock object AV17 in places; the object table number (AV 18) is used here.
Relay control BVs only drive the relays when Lock bit 9 (512) hands the outputs to the BACnet supervisor.
The occupancy section says Lock (AV 18) defaults to 0 (ESI contact in charge), while the Lock examples call 64 the default; read AV 18 on site before relying on BV 14.
